Ombré Leather Parfum by Tom Ford is a Leather fragrance for women and men. Ombré Leather Parfum was launched in 2021. The nose behind this fragrance is Sonia Constant. Top notes are Violet Leaf and Cedar; middle notes are Jasmine Sambac and Orris; base notes are Leather, Woody Notes and Tobacco.

delancy 10/29/25 13:21

Not as (traditionally) masculine-leaning as a lot of the reviews would have you believe. This is a softer take on the DNA of the EDP (which, in itself, isn't exactly the most "butch"- smelling fragrance around, again, despite what people would have you believe).

The added violet makes this very ozonic and easy to wear. I'm not usually a violet fan, but it does work well here in the blend, combined with the creaminess of the orris, lending a softer nature compared to the EDP.

Great for date nights, and the airiness allows this to be worn on summer/spring nights as well, especially in air-conditioned environments. One thing I will say is that I don't think the Ombre Leather DNA is actually as "fool-safe" as an easy go-to first date fragrance as a lot of people say it is. I can see some women genuinely turning their noses up at this DNA: not everyone likes leather as a fragrance note, even when it's portrayed as softly as it is here.

8/10

anas1 08/02/25 10:27

I used to think Ombre Leather was too harsh, almost unwearable—something made only for macho men. But today, I proved myself wrong. When I sprayed it on a tester strip, everything changed.

The opening feels fresh and slightly green, with a subtle brightness that surprised me. As it develops, a sensual touch of jasmine peeks through, softening the edges and adding elegance.

Then comes the drydown—my favorite part. The leather takes center stage, dark and smoky, yet refined and luxurious. It has that rugged charm without being overpowering.

I honestly think this fragrance is perfectly unisex, even if that’s an unpopular opinion. If you’re not into sweet scents, this is a fantastic option. Personally, I still prefer Eau d’Ombre Leather, but this one has definitely earned my respect.
Scent: 8/10
Longevity: 8/10
Sillage: 8/10
Bottle: 8/10
Price: 8/10
Overall: 8/10

The scent profile is amazing here, it's a smooth floral leather just like the EdP but unfortunately the performance is a bad joke! 👎🏻 Even the EdP version lasts longer than this one. 📉

The addition of tobacco, woody notes 🪵and cedar makes Ombre Leather Parfum a bit more masculine than the EdP version. However, they are both floral leathers and you can tell that they were made by a female perfumer (Sonia Constant), and I like the supple softness of it. 💜 💐

cesardiosXO 05/01/25 12:42

I wore this a few days ago layered with Givenchy's Gentleman Society and the combination smells amazing. In any case, Ombré Leather Parfum is a much stronger fragrance so it overpowered Gentleman Society for the entirety of the day, and so I think I can make a review for it on its own.

Ombré Leather Parfum is great, in comparison with the original they're not even in the same planet, this is better in every regard by a country mile. Ombré Leather Parfum immediately opens with a very dense and strong floral leather scent, the leather being smoky and dry to my nose, much like the leather note in a few other leather fragrances I've tried, and unlike the original that smells funky and rotten. Not long after, maybe 2 hours at most, the leather is completely gone and all I'm left with is a very likeable, sweet floral scent that lasts and lasts and lasts forever. Despite it being such a dense and strong fragrance, I didn't find it to be overwhelming but I sprayed very little overall, I'm sure this is a fragrance you should spray lightly, one spray per forearm and two in the neck should be more than enough.

As you can imagine from the previous paragraph, this performs extremely well. ZeaMoore4 04/05/25 16:43

Ombré Leather Parfum is still a dark leather fragrance, but now with a good amount of florals, unlike Ombré Leather EDP, which only Jasmine. Ombré Leather Parfum is more everyday wearable fragrance for the man who's got a little tough and dark side to him. The Ombré Leather EDP always gave me "street thugs" vibes. Ombré Leather Parfum, has more of a "confident man in control, wearing a leather jacket" vibe for me. Its lighter scent with violet leaf and more woody notes makes it less "threatening" so to speak.

Some YouTubers say it's a Suite and tie version of the EDP. But let's be real. If you're wearing a full suit and tie, you don't want to smell like leather. That's silly. Both the EDP and the Parfum are casual to semi-casual. I purchased my bottle to wear when I ride my motorcycle, wearing all my leather motorcycle gear. I used to wear Ombré Leather EDP, but it's a bit much, and i'm not riding like the devil's chasing me anymore.

In the opening, i get leather, violet leaf, and Jasmine. I would Not go as far as calling it aquatic, as stated in the accord list. But I have heard reviews (which i never trust) say it's aquatic or watery. I mostly just get leather and florals.

In the mid, i unfortunately, can get a faint "smoking cigarette" scent. Not an attractive note in anyway. But it does give a slight "bad boy" vibe. It's only present for a short 20 minute period somewhere between 1-2 hours in. Some woods are also more detectable, and tobacco makes itself just a little too apparent for my taste.

Dry-down is mostly woods and leather. And it's Good. It will give anyone within a forearms length a whiff, even 4-6 hours in.

In the very late dry-down (12+ hours and on), it's just Spectacular! Mostly violet leaf, with leather and jasmine underneath it. Lasts for 24+ hours as a skin scent.

Where: casual to semi-casual. Despite what YouTubers say about it being a suite and tie fragrance, I say it's absolutely not.
When: all year, really. Except for the warmest days. Day and night time. Even going out, but Not first dates.
Who: This leans very masculine on me. I'd say age 30's and up will probably be right.

Personal score: 9.5/10. I bought a bottle to wear when I ride my motorcycles during spring, summer, and fall. And for that, it is perfection.

Ombre Leather Parfum is a leathery, floral and woody fragrance.

It has a slightly fresh opening, a little citric and ozonic, although the bitumen leather accord is immediately perceived, like shoe cream. Barfight leather with sunsetting florals blooming into another night of tussles.

Ombre Parfum has been through it on purpose. Still a sweeter leather, but underneath it, musk from heat and confrontation. Driving away from a fight that got you kicked out of the bar, finding a spot to take a breath. A little exhaust and engine oil muddles with jasmine that wasn't expecting company. It hadn't cared to seduce, but in it's nature does. The heat from the day leaves the trees as golden hour wraps up, wafting green cedar through your hair and infusing itself with the cigarette smoke and tobacco already there.

You remember you didn't get to finish your drink, which really pisses you off and you tell yourself you are going back. There are other bars, you can work someone for your next pour. Your sweat is cool and sticks your jacket to you, and you realize if someone messed up that jacket, you WILL go back to the bar. You take it off and examine it. The drinks, the musks, the smoke, and the fight all pour out of it, creating a territorial mark. Exactly what your jacket should do. It's fine. Lucky them.

The little you had of your drink is wearing off, and that adrenaline edge leaves as well. You take a moment with the final flash of sun in the evening blue, putting your jacket back on and taking the last loving drag. You get back in the car, put the day behind you, and head fast into the night.

This is a combined review of Ombre Leather EdP, Ombre Leather Parfum and Eau d'Ombre Leather. I've been looking for a mild and versatile leather fragrance for those occasions where a strong leather scent won't work. Tested from samples. I had really high expectations for these, seeing how well liked they are.

Of the three, I preferred the scent of the EdP the best, although it seemed to be the sweetest of the three (but none are super sweet). The EdP is strictly leather but with the other notes softening it a bit and making it fresher and lighter. Where the EdP fails for me is in performance, specifically longevity. I got maybe about 4 hours out of it at which point it was a very subtle skin scent. I suppose it has been reformulated and watered down. Given the price, I expect much more.

The Parfum had better longevity (around 7 hours) with average sillage. The scent however is less leather. Or, maybe a better way to put it, it's leather plus a woody note and tobacco such that it's not very leather dominant - more of a well blended mix. I cared the least for the Parfum's scent.

Eau d'Ombre is the newest in the collection (released in 2024). It had the best longevity; got about 9 hours out of it. I'm currently at 11 hours and there still remains a very subtle skin scent. It starts out with a strong leathery scent which made be hopeful I had a winner here. I only got maybe about 3 to 4 hours of that. The fragrance then slowly deteriorated into less leather/more vanilla and powdery. Not my style at all.

TL,DR; Didn't care for any of them. The best scent was the EdP but it had dismal performance. The Parfum and Eau d'Ombre had reasonable performance but didn't care for the scent of either.

Tom Ford #7 - A car enthusiast's dream fragrance.

Ombre Leather opens up with a smooth and clean, car interior type leather. The leather note is very dominant at first, but you get hints of a floral, almost fruity sweetness seeping through that is not allowed much spotlight.

I had my 50ml bottle for about a year now, and here are my honest impressions.

When you remove the lid, you get a dense almost chocolate like aroma, which I assume comes from the combination of oris, tobbaco, and the leather accord, so I sometimes just open the bottle and leave it like that in my room.

As to wearing it:
I don't like the opening. Generic cedar with schreechy violet give of a very flat scent, with my some of the woods popping in as well.

Giving it 20 or 30 minutes, the dry down kicks in, with that beautiful smell from opening the cap. Dense jasmine and oriss backed by smooth leather and tobacco. Smells very sweet and dense in a very good way, and lasts around 9 to 10 hours. The projection is solid throughout, going out 1.5 or 2 meters until the or 7th hour where it retracts to arms length, then at the 9 hour mark it becomes a skin scent.

I don't understand why would they use cedar in the opening in that way, but the dry down is certainly worth it.

When to wear: Cold weather evening or special occasions.

Arctic Archer 05/08/24 11:19

Tom Ford's Ombre Leather Perfume (OLP) is a fascinating evolution of the original Ombre Leather (OL), offering a smoother and more refined olfactory experience that elevates its predecessor’s foundation.

While the original Ombre Leather presented itself as an abstract rendition of leather — eschewing the literal interpretations found in scents like Tuscan Leather or, in extreme, Guerlain Cuir Intense (in Ellena’s modern classification, these scents are known as ‘figuratives’, faithful representation of their actual aromas, be it leather, roses or whatever) — instead of OL’s abstract representation, OLP leans into a more tangible leather narrative than OL. It conjures the aroma of a high-quality designer leather jacket, supple and rich, embodying luxury in every note.

OLP distinguishes itself by steering away from the dry, warm, and somewhat harsher qualities so typical of a winter leather scents. Instead, it offers a composition that feels impeccably suited for the transitional seasons of spring and fall. This adaptability stems from its mellow smoothness, which allows it to envelop the wearer in a comforting, yet distinctly sophisticated embrace without overwhelming the senses.

The more pronounced leather quality in OLP does not sacrifice the complexity that fans of the original have come to appreciate. It layers its leathery base with subtle floral, ozonic and spicy notes that enhance its versatility and wearability, making it an excellent choice for both daytime engagements and evening outings. In comparison to the original Ombre Leather, which might be seen as more stark or minimalist, Ombre Leather Perfume is an ode to the nuanced, multi-dimensional aspects of leather, celebrating its depth and richness in a way that feels both innovative and timeless.

Overall, Tom Ford's Ombre Leather Perfume is an exquisite reinterpretation of the brand's leather theme. It provides a softer, yet more vivid leather experience that will likely appeal to those who seek a fragrance that pairs the boldness of leather with a refined, approachable character. For lovers of leather fragrances looking for something that bridges the gap between abstract artistry of OL and wearable fashion, OLP is a compelling choice.

Tom Ford Ombre Leather: When Cologne Becomes the Life of the Party

Get ready to have your nostrils do the conga, because Tom Ford Ombre Leather is not your average fragrance – it's the olfactory disco ball you never knew you needed. If this scent were a dance move, it'd be the moonwalk, because walking forward is so last season.

Uncorking the bottle is like releasing the genie of fabulousness. No wishes granted, just an explosion of leather so suave, James Bond is thinking of trading his tuxedo for a leather jacket. Cardamom and jasmine waltz in like the fragrance equivalent of a power couple, and suddenly, your wrist is hosting the hottest reality show in the fragrance universe.

The leather note is so confident, it's practically telling knock-knock jokes on your skin. You half expect it to whip out a tiny microphone and start a fragrance stand-up routine. "Why did the leather cross the road? To get to the sexier side, obviously."

Patchouli joins the circus, juggling notes like a fragrance maestro. It's like the cool uncle who always brings the good vibes to family gatherings – you didn't know you needed it until it showed up.

And the white moss? It's the mysterious stranger at the party, leaving everyone curious and intrigued. If this fragrance were a detective novel, the white moss would be the twist ending that makes you go, "I did not see that coming, but I'm loving it!"

Wearing Ombre Leather is like being the lead dancer in the fragrance parade. People catch a whiff, and suddenly, you're the grand marshal of the scent carnival. Cue the confetti, because your scent game just won the fragrance Olympics.

In conclusion, Tom Ford Ombre Leather is not just a fragrance; it's a party in a bottle, a comedy roast for your senses, and the VIP pass your nose didn't know it needed. Wear it, and you'll be the life of the fragrance party, leaving everyone wondering, "Is that Ombre Leather, or did a fragrance wizard just cast a spell on that guy?"

MAGNIFICENT!!!
👆 If I had to describe this with one word. Truly a winner.

A couple of years ago, I gave the original Hombre leather a less than favorable review. In it, I mentioned how I didn’t like unisex fragrances (I’ve grown up a bit lol) but I did like the way it smells.
I considered buying it, but wasn’t a fan of how little it projected to me. I needed more horsepower.

Alas, parfum was born. I didn’t hesitate to buy it blind. I figured it would smell more or less the same but more potent.

Upon receiving it, I immediately sprayed my hand and my reaction was… 🤩
I couldn’t have been happier with this blind buy. (Although, you can kinda call it “semi-blind” since I did smell the original before this)

I won’t ramble on about the notes as they clearly display it, it’s in the name, and just read the other people's comments.

It does smell similar to the original Hombre leather. But smoother and more refined.
Kinda like Johnny Walker RED vs Johnny Walker BLACK.

Out of the 100 plus bottles of frags I’ve collected over the years, this is my top three. I genuinely couldn’t wait till cooler weather to wear this. I occasionally sprayed myself while I stayed home (during the warm weather) just to smell this all day.
I am not exaggerating. That is how wonderful this smells.

My ONLY regret is I didn’t buy this sooner and that I didn’t buy two bottles right away (in case there will be batch variations).

Definitely a cooler weather fragrance in my opinion. Although it’s unisex, I wouldn’t want my girl smelling like this.

So is it a safe blind buy?

A• F*CK YES! What’re you waiting for? Buy it now.
B• Go to the store smell it first hand.

First, answer these three questions.

1. Do you deep pockets?
2. Do you prefer the more complex notes in niche fragrances over designers?
3. Do you like leather?
If “YES” to all three questions. See Exhibit A.
If “NO.” See Exhibit B
Otherwise smell it first and see if it has the same impact to you as it did me.

This gets a 10/10

Lastly, if you own a leather jacket… just buy it.

Ombre Leather Parfum is a masterpiece in its genre. It opens with a burst of fresh violet leaf and a refined leather note, that instantly grabs your attention. Its initial opening is not that dissimilar from its EDP forbear. However, as it settles the heart unfolds, revealing an enchanting blend of cedar and jasmine. This composition is lighter and more versatile, but it does not lose its character as a floral woody fragrance throughout its development.

There is a harmonious balance that makes the fragrance very sophisticated and upscale. The sillage is very impressive and leaves an alluring scent trail. There is this sensuous twist at the end of it all, as the leather, woody notes, and tobacco notes merge, adding depth and intrigue to the overall experience. This fragrance is a true masterpiece that takes you through layers of elegance and mystery with every lingering note.

One of my favourites and signature scent-worthy.

You just stepped out of a new Rolls Royce and into the slick marble floored lobby of the elegantly timeless and renowned hotel you've been staying at. You slide into a supple leather armchair to sip your martini and you contemplate visiting the subterranean turkish spa. An older gentleman sitting nearby strikes up a match and lights his pipe. A realistic and comforting leather smell balanced by some floral notes - leans heavily masculine and intense. I once accidentally oversprayed just before a long car journey and gave myself a stomach ache with how intense it was - but even after that I still love it. Autumn_Moon 05/23/22 22:06

It was almost love at first spray.... almost.

I was excited to smell a soft, supple, high-quality leather unfolding on my skin. (Do I want to smell like the interior of a brand-new luxury car? Hmmm... I hadn't thought about it before, but maybe I do!) It was so realistic that I found myself wondering, "Why haven't I tried more perfumes with a leather note before?" The leather was accompanied by a soft floral note -- to me, it resembled jasmine, but it was more of a "processed" and refined representation of jasmine, as opposed to the flower in all its raw, natural glory. Again, this smelled appealing.

And then... ambroxan (or one of its cousins) showed up to the party and crashed it. Amber wasn't listed as a note, so I thought I would be in the clear, but I guess not. (As it turns out, I'm an "ambroxan oversmeller," if you will -- so, this perfume ended up smelling to me like... really awesome, floral leather, but with an ammonia note stomping all over the beautiful experience and interfering with my enjoyment of the rest of the scent. It's not the perfume's fault... it's the way my nose has always been wired. Sigh.)

This could be magical on the right person, so try it if you can. What I was able to experience of it felt like it could suit anyone -- there's leather, yes (very, very expensive leather), but the floral aspect is also present, and this prevents the fragrance from becoming "solely the smell of leather in a vehicle upholstery workshop" and helps to balance things out. The performance is also out-of-this-world in terms of longevity -- one dozen scrubbings later, I could still catch whiffs of it. If only it were for me...
